sentences.text:
on 16 December, 2023
 The Honourable Sri Justice K.Surender
 Criminal Petition No.12391 Of 2023
Order:

Criminal Petition is filed by the petitioners - accused Nos.1 to 3 to quash the proceedings in C.C.No.2398 of 2020 on the file of the learned III Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Nampally, Hyderabad.

entities.text: III Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Nampally, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Petitioners were summoned to face trial for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 405 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC').
2.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned Assistant Public Prosecutor, appearing for respondent No.1 - State.
Perused the record.

3. The complainant filed a private complaint before the learned III Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Hyderabad, wherein the learned Magistrate having examined the complainant and recording sworn statement, the learned Magistrate had taken cognizance against the petitioners on 04.02.2020.

entities.text: III Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The order reads thus:
'Complainant absent.
Perused the averments in the complaint, the sworn statement of the complainant and copies of documents filed on behalf of the complainant.
Prima facie, case is made out against the accused for the offence u/s 420 r/w 34 IPC.
Hence, the case is taken on file against the accused for the offence u/s 420 r/w 34 of IPC.
Issue summons to accused on payment of process.

As seen from the said order, the learned Magistrate has not recorded any reasons as to what promted the learned Magistrate to take cognizance against the petitioners and how the offences are prima facie made out against them.
5. Issuance of summons in a criminal case is a serious issue and without giving reasons, the petitioners cannot be summoned to face criminal trial.
Unless the criminal Court finds adequate grounds and reasons to summon the accused, the same cannot be done.
As seen from the docket order of the learned Magistrate, it was ordered to issue summons to accused without there being a prima facie satisfaction of the ingredients of the offence.
It appears that the Magistrate has mechanically directed issuance of summons.
6. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sunil Bharti Mittal v. Central Bureau of Investigation 1 held that the order of issuing process to accused to face criminal trial is a serious issue.

entities.text: Sunil Bharti Mittal v. Central Bureau of Investigation 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Such summoning cannot be done on mere asking and the Court has to record reasons for summoning a person.

In GHCL Employees Stock Option Trust M/S. Smart Login Solutions Private ... vs The State Of Telangana on 16 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199575152/
1 v. India Infoline Limited 2, the Hon'ble Supreme Court found fault with the order of the Magistrate in issuing summons when the Magistrate has not recorded his satisfaction about the prima facie case against the accused.

entities.text: GHCL Employees Stock Option Trust M/S. Smart Login Solutions Private ... vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Chief Enforcement Officer v. Videocon International Limited 3, the Hon'ble Supreme Court while discussing the expression 'cognizance' held that in criminal law 'cognizance' means becoming aware of and the word used with respect to Court or a Judge initiating proceedings in respect of an offence.

entities.text: Chief Enforcement Officer v. Videocon International Limited 3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Taking cognizance would involve application of mind by the Magistrate to the suspected commission of an offence.
(2015) 4 Supreme Court Cases 609 (2013) 4 SCC 505 (2008) 2 SCC 492 7.

In Fakhruddin Ahmad v. State of Uttaranchal and another 4 it is held as follows:
"17.Nevertheless, it is well settled that before a Magistrate can be said to have taken cognizance of an offence, it is imperative that he must have taken notice of the accusations and applied his mind to the allegations made in the complaint or in the police report or the information received from a source other than a police report, as the case may be, and the material filed therewith.

entities.text: Fakhruddin Ahmad v. State of Uttaranchal and another 4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It needs little emphasis that it is only when the Magistrate applies his mind and is satisfied that the allegations, if proved, would constitute an offence and decides to initiate proceedings against the alleged offender, that it can be positively stated that he has taken cognizance of the offence.

Cognizance is in regard to the offence and not the offender."
8.

In view of the observations and directions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the judgments referred to supra, the act of issuing process and summoning the accused to face criminal trial is a serious issue and such orders directing summons to a person to face criminal trial cannot be on the basis of cryptic orders and it should be an order reflecting application of mind by the Presiding Officer while taking cognizance and issuing process.
(2008) 17 Supreme Court Cases 157 9.
Though elaborate discussion is not required for the purpose of issuing summons, the order taking cognizance should reflect that the Presiding Officer has grasp of the case.

The contents of either the charge sheet/private complaint/protest petition are understood by the Presiding Officer and the cognizance orders should reflect that there is a prima facie case stating facts very precisely to summon the accused or refer a case for the purpose of investigation or set aside the findings of investigation and summon the accused.
10. Judicial orders cannot be cryptic or vague or bald assertion that an offence is made out.

It would not suffice to merely mention that cognizance is taken or that mere mentioning that the Presiding Officer is satisfied on the basis of the record that it is a fit case to take cognizance and issue summons.

When the order does not reflect even briefly what the case is about, it is apparent that the Presiding Officer has not applied his mind judicially to the facts of the case before summoning the accused to face criminal trial and the orders are mechanically passed without even considering M/S. Smart Login Solutions Private ... vs The State Of Telangana on 16 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199575152/
2

entities.text: M/S. Smart Login Solutions Private ... vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: whether the allegations or the contents of such charge sheets/complaints make out a prima facie case.

11. Since the cognizance order dated 04.03.2020 of the learned Magistrate lacks reasons and it does not appear that the learned Magistrate has applied mind in issuance of summons, the same is set aside.

12. Accordingly, the Criminal Petition is allowed and the proceedings against the petitioners in C.C.No.2398 of 2020 on the file of the learned III Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Nampally, Hyderabad are hereby quashed.

entities.text: III Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Nampally, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: However, this order will not preclude the trial Court from taking cognizance by giving reasons.
Consequently, miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.

JUSTICE K.SURENDER Date: 16.12.2023 ns M/S. Smart Login Solutions Private ... vs The State Of Telangana on 16 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199575152/
